issue: Is an alien excused from proving the exhaustion and deprivation-of-judicial-review prongs of 8 U.S.C. § 1326(d) in a collateral attack on a removal order when the immigration judge did not inform him of his eligibility for discretionary relief such as voluntary departure?

sides.position: The alien is excused from establishing the first prong (exhaustion) and satisfies the second (deprivation of judicial review) when he was not informed of his eligibility for discretionary relief.
cases: United States v. Sosa, 387 F.3d 131 (2d Cir. 2004)
United States v. Ubaldo-Figueroa, 364 F.3d 1042 (9th Cir. 2004)

sides.position: The alien has not satisfied, and is not excused from, establishing the first two prongs of § 1326(d) when he was not informed of his eligibility for discretionary relief.
cases: Richardson v. United States, 558 F.3d 216 (3d Cir. 2009)
United States v. Cordova-Soto, 804 F.3d 714 (5th Cir. 2015)
United States v. Chavez-Alonso, 431 F.3d 726 (10th Cir. 2005)

quote: This question is the subject of a circuit split that we haven’t yet weighed in on.
cite: United States v. Lexy Herrera-Pagoada, 14 F.4th 311 (4th Cir. 2021)
